key_insight: Q-Capsule reduces barren-plateau risk by localizing each capsule’s observable support, limiting inter-capsule entanglement, and growing depth adaptively with QFIM feedback.
engineering_relevance: The architecture offers a practical route to trainable quantum neural networks that scale better in width while using fewer two-qubit gates and measurements.
method: Partition the qubit register into capsules with local readout.
Use sparse inter-capsule coupling plus trainable data re-uploading.
Grow circuit depth adaptively using QFIM-guided policy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports stable gradient variance versus exponential suppression in global baselines, and adaptive training reaches 98.1% binary and 97.7% four-class accuracy with about 73% fewer two-qubit gates on the multiclass task.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on careful capsule partitioning and hardware noise levels may still affect the benefit of deeper or more connected circuits.
paper_title: Q-Capsule: A Localized Capsule-Based Quantum Neural Architecture for Barren Plateau Mitigation
